I'm mapping out the grid layout, marking which cells are walls, open spaces, and the arms extending from the 3 marker so I can flood fill from its position at row 2, column 7.

Now I'm tracing the BFS outward: the neighbors above, below, and to the left of the starting point are all step-1 arm cells, since the cell to the right is blocked by a wall.

Continuing the BFS expansion, I keep propagating distances outward through steps 6 to 13, tracking which cells get newly assigned distance values as the frontier grows in multiple directions, including branches near (10,9) and (10,6).

Continuing the fill through steps 22-26, most branches dead-end quickly against walls. I'm now checking whether the region around (4,0)-(4,5) got reached at all, since (3,5) is a wall blocking that column from the earlier fill path.

Tracing further, (5,5) connects to (6,5), which leads up through (6,6),(6,7),(7,7),(8,7) — a whole branch that's only reachable via (5,5)-(4,5), which our fill never touched. But I notice (10,6) links back up to this region through (9,6), so it may actually connect elsewhere after all.

Now I'm checking the left component around row 4 columns 0-5: it connects to (5,5),(6,5) then dead-ends at (8,7), and separately down through (4,0)-(3,0)-(2,0)-(1,0)-(0,0), which is blocked. Since nothing reached links into this cluster, it stays unfilled — I'm now shifting to check column 13 on the right side for similar dead zones, tracing rows 4 through 12 to see if any of those cells connect back to the reached region.

I'm tracing whether this whole lower region connects back to the fill, checking chains through rows 8-14 around columns 7-13, and noting that (10,11) was already reached at step 11, which links this cluster into the main fill.

I'm checking whether this region connects to the large set of already-reached cells across the grid, comparing coordinates one by one to see if any overlap exists.

Checking that region too, it connects to the (12,7) area on the right, so it stays unreached. Then I trace the cluster near (8,0)-(10,3): (8,3) is actually reached, but its neighbors (9,3) and (8,2) are walls, so I need to verify whether the (10,1)-(10,3) chain links back into the reached area through any open cell.

Working through it, that chain forms its own isolated component with no connection to reached cells, so it scores 0. The pair at (0,4)-(0,5) is similarly boxed in by walls on all sides, giving another isolated 0. I confirm (12,0)-(12,1) are already reached, then move on to scanning the remaining unexplored cells around (6,5)-(8,7) and the (0-4,0-5) block, which all appear to be 0 as well.

Now I'm assigning colors by alternating 3 and 7 based on step parity, tracing the BFS layers outward from (2,7) through the grid until I reach around step 16 near (8,...).

Once the coloring assignment is complete, I start constructing the output grid row by row, filling in each cell value based on the computed positions.

Continuing to fill in the grid values row by row, tracking the pattern across rows 6 through 11.

Continuing the BFS expansion through depths 11 and 12, I'm tracing which cells stay alive versus which branches die out as the frontier spreads across the grid.

Continuing the BFS expansion, I keep pushing frontier cells outward through distances 14, 15, and 16, marking new zero-cost cells and identifying dead ends where obstacles block further propagation.

Continuing the BFS expansion through distances 19 and 20, several branches dead-end while others push forward toward row 0's edge cells.

Continuing the BFS distance expansion through the grid, several branches die out while others open new frontiers at distances 24-26, tracking which cells remain reachable versus blocked.

Continuing the BFS expansion, the frontier keeps advancing along the open path through generations 29 to 35, tracing dead ends at (6,6), (0,0), and (9,1) while pushing forward through (5,0), (6,0), (7,0), (8,0), and branching to (8,1), (8,2), and (9,0).

That path dead-ends. I'm now cross-checking which cells remain unvisited by scanning row by row, and rows 0 and 1 turn out fully covered already.

(2,18) stays as a zero since all its neighbors are unvisited eights, so it's isolated. I'm continuing this same distance-fill sweep through rows 3 through 6, tracking each cell's value against its neighbors.

I'm tracing whether the zero-region around rows 8-10, columns 18-22 connects back to the already-visited region near (4,22), checking each neighboring cell's value to determine connectivity.

Continuing to trace distances through rows 9 and 10, filling in unvisited columns, then setting up the coloring rule: even distances map to one color, odd distances to another, and I start assigning these values row by row for the output grid.

I catch a potential inconsistency in row 0 where two adjacent cells both have odd distance 13, which shouldn't happen if the coloring alternates properly along the path—so I go back to double-check whether (0,13)'s actual distance should be 14 instead, tracing the predecessor chain again.

Rechecking the row 0 chain from column 14 outward: distances step up by one each cell going both directions, continuing symmetrically through columns 15-22 and down into rows 1-4 at column 22. I also verify a parallel chain along column 20 and start rechecking another branch near (7,10) working backward toward row 0.

Continuing the distance computation, I'm noticing I need to double-check my earlier value for (2,10) since the chain leading to it doesn't seem consistent with what I calculated before - I should go back and verify that particular path.

Continuing the distance calculations further out, I confirm my earlier listing was mostly right aside from some off-by-one spots, and now I'm re-deriving the chain around column 14 and the 18-20 region to double-check consistency.

Continuing to trace out the distance layers across the grid, mapping which coordinates fall at each increasing radius from the center point out to distance 25.

Now that I have the full distance map, I'm assigning colors based on parity of the distance value: even distances get color 7, odd distances get color 4, and I'm starting to fill in row 0's cells with these assignments.

Continuing to fill in rows 2 and 3, computing each cell's value based on distance-to-target rules, though I notice one cell in row 2 is unvisited and gets marked 0.

I'm now working through row 4's grid values the same way, mapping cell indices to computed distances, then starting row 5 with c0 mapped to 7.

Continuing to trace through rows 7 and 8, updating each cell's value based on visited/unvisited status and distance calculations.

Finishing row10 with the remaining zeros, then row11 is all 8s. I catch an error at row9 c10, which should be 7 not 4, and correct it, then double-check a few other cells against their diagonal values to confirm the pattern holds.
